page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a burstable, budget-oriented virtual machine instance belonging to the f1 server family. It features a single shared vCPU mapped to an Intel Xeon processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 0.6 GB of system memory and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. CPU features include AVX and AVX512F instruction sets, alongside a 38 MB L3 cache.

Performance benchmarks place the f1-micro in the lower tier of cloud compute resources. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield a score of 384.79, while the PassMark CPU score is 236.08, both falling into the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 80.8 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 0.2 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is measured at 0.22 GB/sec.

Due to its shared-core architecture and minimal memory footprint, the f1-micro offers high qualitative cost efficiency for low-intensity, intermittent tasks. However, its resource constraints present significant tradeoffs for sustained or memory-heavy applications. This server is best suited for lightweight utility tasks, basic web serving, development testing, and simple cron jobs rather than database hosting or high-throughput production workloads.
